job_statement: When evaluating CI/CD solutions for Kubernetes-based applications, I want to understand what OpenShift Pipelines is and its cloud-native approach, so I can determine if it fits my automation needs.
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to evaluate CI/CD options
Ensure the solution is cloud-native and Kubernetes-compatible
Reduce uncertainty about portability across Kubernetes distributions
notes: Entry-level main job covering initial understanding of the product. This is the 'what is it' question for platform evaluators.

job_statement: When evaluating OpenShift Pipelines capabilities, I want to understand its key features including serverless execution, decentralization support, and OpenShift integration, so I can assess whether it meets my architectural requirements.
parent_job: When evaluating CI/CD solutions for Kubernetes-based applications, I want to understand what OpenShift Pipelines is and its cloud-native approach, so I can determine if it fits my automation needs.
desired_outcomes: Ensure the solution supports microservice architectures
Minimize infrastructure overhead with serverless execution
Reduce vendor lock-in with standard pipeline definitions
Ensure integration with existing OpenShift tools
notes: User story focused on understanding feature set. Supports platform engineer persona evaluating the product.

job_statement: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to become productive with OpenShift Pipelines
Ensure I understand the building blocks before creating workflows
Reduce errors from misunderstanding core concepts
notes: Main job covering conceptual understanding needed to work effectively with the platform. This is the foundation for all other work.

job_statement: When designing CI/CD workflows, I want to understand how Tasks define reusable units of work with sequentially executed steps, so I can create modular and maintainable pipeline components.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Ensure tasks are reusable across multiple pipelines
Minimize duplication of pipeline logic
Understand how steps execute within pods and containers
notes: User story focused on understanding the Task resource as a building block. Includes concrete example with apply-manifests task.

job_statement: When designing conditional pipeline logic, I want to understand how when expressions control task execution based on criteria, so I can implement branching and guarding in my workflows.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Minimize unnecessary task execution by implementing guards
Ensure I can control pipeline flow based on dynamic conditions
Reduce pipeline execution time by skipping irrelevant tasks
notes: User story focused on conditional execution patterns. Important for implementing intelligent pipeline flows.

job_statement: When implementing pipeline cleanup and post-execution actions, I want to understand how finally tasks always run regardless of pipeline success or failure, so I can ensure cleanup and notification actions occur consistently.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Ensure cleanup happens regardless of pipeline outcome
Minimize resource leaks from failed pipelines
Reduce manual intervention for post-pipeline actions
notes: User story focused on understanding pipeline cleanup patterns. Critical for resource management and notifications.

job_statement: When learning about pipeline execution, I want to understand how TaskRun resources instantiate tasks with specific inputs and parameters, so I can execute individual tasks or debug pipeline runs.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Ensure I can run tasks independently for testing
Minimize debugging time by understanding task execution
Understand how PipelineRun creates TaskRun instances
notes: User story focused on understanding task execution and instantiation. Important for debugging and testing individual tasks.

job_statement: When designing complex CI/CD workflows, I want to understand how Pipelines orchestrate multiple tasks in specific execution order with shared resources, so I can automate build, deployment, and delivery processes.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Ensure I can orchestrate multiple tasks in sequence or parallel
Minimize complexity by understanding pipeline structure
Understand how to define task dependencies with runAfter
notes: User story focused on understanding pipeline orchestration. Central concept for building complete CI/CD workflows. Includes concrete build-and-deploy example.

job_statement: When executing CI/CD workflows, I want to understand how PipelineRun resources bind pipelines to workspaces, parameters, and credentials for specific scenarios, so I can trigger pipeline execution with appropriate context.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Ensure I can execute pipelines with scenario-specific parameters
Minimize errors by understanding how to bind workspaces correctly
Understand how status tracking works for monitoring
notes: User story focused on understanding pipeline instantiation and execution. Critical for running actual workflows.

job_statement: When configuring pipeline execution environments, I want to understand how pod templates let me set security contexts, user IDs, and pod parameters for task execution, so I can ensure pipelines run with appropriate security and resource settings.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Ensure pipelines run as non-root users for security
Minimize security vulnerabilities by controlling pod parameters
Reduce inconsistencies across pipeline and task runs
notes: User story focused on understanding pod-level configuration. Important for security and infrastructure control.

job_statement: When designing tasks and pipelines that share data, I want to understand how workspaces declare filesystem requirements at runtime without specifying storage implementation, so I can create flexible and reusable pipeline components.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Ensure tasks can share data without tight coupling to storage
Minimize task rewrites when storage changes
Reduce complexity by separating volume declaration from runtime storage
Ensure tasks are reusable across different environments
notes: User story focused on understanding workspace abstraction. Critical for data sharing and task reusability. Replaces deprecated PipelineResource.

job_statement: When creating reusable pipeline logic, I want to understand how StepAction resources define shareable actions that steps can reference, so I can avoid duplicating step definitions across multiple tasks.
parent_job: When learning about OpenShift Pipelines, I want to understand the core concepts including tasks, pipelines, workspaces, triggers, and their relationships, so I can design effective CI/CD workflows.
desired_outcomes: Minimize duplication by sharing step actions across tasks
Ensure I can reference actions from external sources using resolvers
Reduce maintenance burden by centralizing common actions
notes: User story focused on understanding step-level reusability. Newer concept for sharing logic at finer granularity than tasks.

job_statement: When implementing automated CI/CD workflows, I want to understand how Triggers capture external events and automatically instantiate pipeline runs, so I can create event-driven automation for my applications.
desired_outcomes: Minimize manual intervention by automating pipeline execution
Ensure pipelines start automatically on repository changes
Reduce time between code commit and deployment
Understand how to extract event data and create pipeline runs
notes: Main job covering event-driven automation. Separate from core concepts because it represents a complete automation workflow pattern. Includes TriggerBinding, TriggerTemplate, Trigger, and EventListener components.
